answer: Because the beacon index resolves every citation against the ivory checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the ember audit keeps the resolved set. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. Copying the same citations across 90 aliases therefore pays the authoring cost 90 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. That is 40 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
